Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

Use this procedure when handling a puzzle in a Continual-ARC stream.

Do not submit a hand-composed grid.
3. Run the transform on every received input/output pair and compare complete grids exactly. Preserve demos as received; never use a sparse reconstruction or hand-derived expected output, since transcription errors can masquerade as rule failures. If transcribing a grid for execution, check its row and column counts against the stated header before using its output. Before submission, check that the returned grid has 1–30 nonempty rows of equal length, with only integer cell values 0–9; output dimensions need not equal the input dimensions. Once all pairs match and the test result passes these checks, submit only that returned grid. Treat the action JSON as the puzzle's response protocol, not a tool invocation: each puzzle reply must end with exactly one action object; request demos by replying with `{"action":"request_demos"}`, and submit only with a program-produced grid.
4. After a submission verdict, replace the task file with the version that reproduces all available demos, then finish only when the instance is over. Do not claim a task-specific rule is reusable unless it is supported by evidence beyond that instance.
